To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the activity of a rat liver microsome and supernatant fraction for N-demethyla-tion of meperidine is increased by use of a loose type homogenizer, high substrate concentration, and a higher concentration of buffer in the homogenization solution.
the N-demethy-lase system is a microsome plus supernate fraction system and that the N-demethylase system is inhibited by starvation and by a TPNase or TPN inhibitor.

the N-demethy-lase activity of starved liver microsomes is restored by glucose 6-phos-phate or isocitric acid, and that the N-demethylase activity of normal liver microsomes can be inhibited by the microsomes from starved livers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a new assay system for the measurement of the N-demethylating activity of liver microsomes and the effect of starvation and of various substrates on this activity.
the metabolism of narcotic drugs and the factors which may affect the metabolism.
the study of an N-demethylase which has been found to be present in the combined microsomes plus supernatant fractions of liver from rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
starvation of rats results in an inhibition of N-demethylation by a mechanism which is not yet understood, and that this inhibition can be reversed in vitro.
starvation of rats for 16 hours results in the appearance of a TPNase or TPN inactivating system in the microsomes of rat liver.
the system for N-demethyiation of meperidine is not a single enzyme but a complex of enzymes which are dependent upon each other for optimal functioning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the N-demethylase system in the microsome plus supernant fraction of rat hepatic cells is a complex system which requires for its optimal functioning, in addition to substrate, cofactor and microsome, an adequate supply of energy in the form of a high energy phosphate compound.
the N-demethylase system in rat liver consists of two parts, a TPN-requiring enzyme and a TPN-regenerating system.
the activity of the N-demethylating enzyme system is dependent on the presence of a cofactor which is not a TPN or a TPNase, and is not glucose 6-phospate, isocitrate or a TPN-regenerating system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N-demethylase system in rat liver is very sensitive to nutritional status and that it is probably not a good model for detoxication in man.
starvation for as little as sixteen hours reduces the ability of the rat liver to N-demethylate the narcotic drug, meperidine.
we have developed a new and highly sensitive method for assaying the N-demethyation of meperidine.
